text.p: World number one Pete Sampras looked every inch the champion on Saturday as he demolished doubles specialist Mark Woodforde 6-1 6-0 6-1 to reach the last 16 of the Australian Open.

In front of a raucous centre court crowd, who soon realised Australia's last singles hope did not have a chance, Sampras produced textbook serves and fierce forehands to wrap up the match in one hour and 19 minutes.
Woodforde, a 31-year-old who has won almost every honour in the game in men's doubles, was a surprise semifinalist in Melbourne last year. He is ranked 28th in the world.
Two other Australians, Woodforde's doubles partner Todd Woodbridge and Scott Draper, also lost third-round ties at the Open. Sampras's next opponent will be the unseeded Dominik Hrbaty of Slovakia.
